_comment: An excluded item is removed from BOTH numerator and denominator, listed by ID with its
reason, and counted as a headline number. Exclusions exist because the corpus builder
was told to flag anything it was unsure was genuinely defective versus arguably
compliant, and a bad test item scored either way is worse than no test item.
1. An exclusion filed AFTER the first scored run requires a dated written
justification, which is printed in the report. Filing exclusions while looking at
results is how a corpus becomes whatever the arms happened to find.
2. If exclusions reach 20% of planted defects the experiment is INCONCLUSIVE (§6.8):
too much of the corpus has been removed for the remainder to represent it.
This file is hashed into FREEZE.json.
